version.changelog:
**Major update: MoltGuard onboarding, UX, and command workflow simplified for instant agent protection.**

- New onboarding: Installs with zero intervention, auto-registers, and activates protection immediately (500 free detections/day).
- Streamlined user instructions focus on immediate installation, no configuration required.
- Updated guidance: Users/testers prompted to verify protection by running a live, built-in security test.
- Introduced `/og_status`, `/og_sanitize`, `/og_config`, `/og_claim`, `/og_core`, and `/og_dashboard` commands for easier status, configuration, and management.
- All security detections now performed by Core (cloud-based), with clear explanations of detected risks and user notifications.
- Documentation condensed and clarified for non-expert users; advanced provenance and config topics remain as reference.

llm.summary: The skill is internally consistent with being a runtime security plugin that registers an agent with OpenGuardrails Core and stores a local API key; nothing requests unrelated secrets or strange system access, but there are a few minor inconsistencies and you should verify network behavior before trusting it.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (a runtime security plugin) align with the included scripts and documentation: the skill registers an agent, stores credentials under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/, and sends sanitized tool metadata to openguardrails.com/core for cloud classification. Required binaries/env vars are none, which is proportionate to the described functionality.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs the agent/user to install the plugin, restart the gateway, read sample files (to demonstrate detection), and run commands like /og_status, /og_config, etc. Those instructions stay within the stated security purpose. Minor inconsistency: the prose sometimes claims "auto-registers" and "no configuration needed," but the shipped scripts (activate.mjs) show an explicit registration flow (POST /api/v1/agents/register) and credentials saved locally — it's plausible registration happens during install, but that is not shown in the provided code. The skill also instructs the agent to relay quota-exceeded messages in full, which could reveal message text to users but is consistent with a billing/notification flow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No external install spec is included (instruction-only). The bundle contains two small helper scripts (activate/status) that operate on the user's home directory. No downloads from untrusted URLs or archive extraction were included. This is lower risk than remote download installs, but you should still verify the package source before running node scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables or unrelated credentials are requested. The skill stores an API key/agent id under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json and sends only sanitized tool metadata to the Core service per the docs. That is proportionate for a cloud-assisted security product. The documentation claims local sanitization of secrets/PII before transmission; if you have high privacy concerns, verify sanitization behavior in the published source before enabling cloud detection.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default autonomy are used. The skill writes only to its own credential directory under the user's home (~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/), which is expected. It does not request system-wide configuration changes or other skills' credentials in the provided files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This package appears to do what it claims: local protections plus optional cloud classification via openguardrails.com/core, saving an agent API key under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/. Before installing: 1) Verify the package provenance (npm and GitHub links in references) and compare the published tarball to the GitHub source as suggested in references/details.md. 2) Inspect the code (especially any larger plugin package you install) to confirm local sanitization is implemented before any outbound network calls. 3) Monitor network calls (tcpdump/mitmproxy/Little Snitch) during activation to confirm traffic only goes to the expected domain (openguardrails.com/core). 4) If you’re uncomfortable with cloud-assisted detection, keep the skill unregistered (the docs claim local-only protections until registration) or delete ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json to revoke access. Note the small documentation inconsistency: SKILL.md sometimes says "auto-registers"/"no configuration needed" while the included activate script shows an explicit registration step — confirm whether the plugin auto-runs registration on install in your environment before trusting fully.
